absent: Layout and semantics of task restart container beyond event word, including user pointer, cached identifiers, signature and slice state.
Detection of newer versus legacy ABI generation and resume notification raising mechanism.
Timer arming implementation, expiry duration configuration, static keys and deferred handling.
Scheduler placement, topology lookup, signal forcing and tracepoint implementation details.
User restart and critical section record layouts and full syscall and control operation semantics.
Guard, user access, branch prediction and checking helper implementations.

findings.text: The event record packs transient and persistent restart state into overlapping views sharing 64 bits. One view shows a single integer, another splits it into a 32 bit transient word plus registration, padding and error portions. The transient word carries three single byte markers for schedule switch, identifier change and user interrupt entry. A separate byte records registration presence. The error portion appears both as a 16 bit value and as two single byte indicators for fatal failure and slowpath need.

Statistics aggregate unsigned long counters for return to user activity and slice extension outcomes. Tallies cover exits, signal deliveries, slow and fast handling, identifier refreshes, critical section processing, clear operations and fixup operations, together with granted, expired, revoked, yielded and aborted slice transitions.
The registration version field reserves its low eight bits as a mask with decimal value 255.

Duplication distinguishes shared address spaces from private ones. When the new task shares memory with its parent its restart state is cleared through a shared reset helper that zeroes the container and marks the CPU identifier uninitialized. Otherwise the child receives a copy of the parent state. Exec reuses the same reset helper. Reset runs under interrupt saving protection against preemption and cross processor barrier work.
Allocation alignment is a power of two derived from the size implied by the end member offset inside the user restart record.

Build variation is expressed through alternative macro bodies. Counter increment expands to a preempt aware per processor increment in one configuration, a raw per processor increment in another, and an empty statement in the third. An inline marker expands either to nothing or to a forced inline attribute. Each header defines its own include guard constant.

Tracing helpers execute only when the corresponding trace facility is active, with identifier update tracing additionally requiring a non null identifier record. Active cases delegate to underlying implementations for update reporting and for fixup reporting with fault address and range data. Inactive builds expose empty helpers with matching signatures.

User interrupt entry is recorded for the current task only on generic entry builds, otherwise the recorder is empty. Dedicated flag testing either masks the work word for the sequence bit or unconditionally reports work when the bit is unavailable, with clearing either resetting the thread flag after asserting separation from resume notification or doing nothing. Syscall exit tallies an exit and under checking builds warns if a switch marker survived before clearing all transient markers. Interrupt exit tallies, asserts absence of a switch marker, and clears markers to cover interrupts that did not schedule.

Switch handling depends on ABI generation. The newer generation records a switch and requests resume notification only when at least one of the user interrupt marker or the identifier change marker is set, relying on the newer mode to imply registration. The legacy generation always marks identifiers changed plus switch occurred whenever registration is present, then requests notification. Dedicated helpers allow explicitly marking identifiers changed, forcing both markers plus notification for the current registered task, and re requesting notification on virtualized user exit when a switch remains pending on builds without generic flag bits.

Slice extension availability is governed by a global static key, with disabled builds reporting unavailable and empty helpers. When available, timer arming succeeds only if the current task holds a granted state, otherwise it reports no work. Clearing the kernel grant resets the granted indicator and optionally tallies a revocation when statistics and a prior grant coincide. Clearing the user control writes zero to the user control word when globally enabled. Grant evaluation requires both task enablement and user interrupt entry, rejects when extra thread work is pending or a grant already exists by clearing user and kernel state, otherwise consumes a pending user request, records granted status with an expiry derived from a configured duration plus monotonic time, clears task and preempt rescheduling markers under interrupt protection, and rearms deferred timer handling under the same protection. User access faults during evaluation force a segmentation signal and report failure.

Return to user processing starts from a pending switch marker that also implies registration. When no switch is pending all transient markers are cleared and no further work occurs. When pending, a fast tally is taken and identifier handling runs. If identifiers are unchanged only the user critical section address is fetched and slice state cleared, with deeper handling only in debug mode or when an address is present. If changed, fresh placement derived identifiers for processor, node and memory context are written to user memory while fetching the critical section address and clearing slice state, caching the new values and reporting update activity. Critical section handling is skipped when entry lacked user interrupt context unless debug mode forces it. Failures mark slowpath need and request resume notification; success clears the dedicated flag and all transient markers before attempting timer arming.

Reset holds an interrupt saving guard across zeroing to serialize against preemption and cross processor barrier interrupts. Grant evaluation holds an interrupt guard while clearing task and preempt rescheduling markers so the pair stays atomic against local interrupts and scheduler interprocessor interrupts. Successful grant handling holds the same guard while rearming deferred timer state. Exit to user identifier handling disables page faults because it runs with interrupts disabled.

User descriptors are checked against the task address limit with overflow protection. Debug handling additionally requires start ordering relative to the current instruction location, abort placement outside the described range, zero version and flags, signature match sampled from before the abort location, address validity for the signature read, and user interrupt context where tracked. Standard handling requires user range for descriptor and abort addresses plus signature match, leaving other misuse to user consequences. Identifier refresh in debug or newer ABI modes verifies that user visible identifier fields match cached kernel values before overwriting. Validation failure marks the event fatal. User read or write faults abort the operation with failure, and slice grant faults additionally force a segmentation signal.

Public integration surface includes switch notification, identifier change marking, forced update, virtualized exit handling, fork and exec handling, slowpath and signal delivery hooks, generic syscall hook, slice extension control and timer helpers, trace and statistics helpers, plus exit to user restart and cleanup helpers, with empty variants provided when support is compiled out.

Kernel entry integration points cover slowpath handling, signal delivery, syscall handling and return to user restart. Disabled builds implement each as a no effect operation, with restart reporting no further work and slice control reporting unsupported. Enabled restart checks a dedicated flag where available, runs identifier and critical section refresh on pending switch, records slowpath and requests resume notification on failure, clears the dedicated flag on success, and finally attempts slice timer arming before returning to user.
